To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel approach to multiclass spectral clustering that is robust, efficient and nearly optimal.
We present an efficient and principled approach for multi-class spectral clustering.
multiclass spectral clustering can be formulated as a continuous relaxation followed by a discrete approximation and the resulting method is robust to initialization and fast in convergence.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) What is the role of the eigenvectors in multiclass spectral clustering? (2) How to solve a discrete multiclass clustering problem? (3) What is the relationship between spectral clustering and other clustering algorithms?

the following problems: (i) How do we cluster data with multiple classes? (ii) How do we solve a discrete clustering problem by eigen-decompositions? and (iii) How do we discretize continuous solutions to obtain discrete solutions?

the following problems: (1) How do we solve the multiclass spectral clustering problem efficiently? (2) How do we compute the optimal discrete solution? (3) How can we guarantee that the solution is nearly global-optimal?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach is an excellent solution for multiclass spectral clustering, and that the authors have done a great job in presenting it.
the method is robust to initialization, fast, and produces nearly optimal solutions.
our method provides a novel approach to multiclass spectral clustering, and that it is competitive with state-of-the-art methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have a new way of thinking of multiclass spectral clustering.
we have developed a principled account of multiclass spectral clustering, with theoretical guarantees and practical improvements.
we have proposed an efficient, principled, and provably optimal method for multiclass spectral clustering.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the eigenvectors are not just a by-product of the eigen-decomposition, but rather the generators of all optimal solutions.
the discrete solutions can be obtained efficiently by solving a relaxed continuous optimization, which in turn provides the generator of all optimal clustering solutions.
multiclass clustering is not a difficult problem, and that it is best solved by a simple eigen-decomposition.
